dataset.license_or_access_note: Existing research authorization confirmed by the project owner; no public release performed.

original_annotations: On YouTube, open a cooking tutorial that demonstrates the same method as in the video. This existing prompt is a location cue, not the visual ground truth.

observed_events.description: A round browned bread cooks on the flat griddle; the wearer then rolls an opaque round dough disk on the floured counter beside the same dough supply and a pan of yellow coarse mixture. The disk interior is not visible in this released packet.
The wearer forms a small dough piece into a hollow cup in the left hand.
The wearer takes several spoonfuls of the coarse yellow mixture from the nearby pan and puts them inside the hollow dough cup.
The wearer gathers the filled dough edges, pinches the opening closed and rounds the sealed filled dough by hand. The mixture is enclosed within the dough, not served as a topping or side.

supported_claims.text: The initial released packet shows flatbread preparation but does not establish whether the dough contains filling. The yellow mixture beside the work area does not by itself prove it goes inside the bread.
The later packet shows filling being put inside the dough and the rim being gathered to enclose it, establishing a stuffed flatbread preparation.
The same cooker, dough supply, rolling area and adjacent mixture pan persist; later frames reveal the method in the same cooking session rather than a language change or a new independent request.

construct.research_question: Can later visual evidence of filling and sealing dough correct an initially broad flatbread choice, while retaining any initially chosen guide that already teaches the filled preparation?
construct.belief_before: V0 establishes solid-dough flatbread preparation and rolling. The opaque disk does not reveal whether it is filled, so either a reviewed plain or stuffed flatbread method can be an initial reasonable choice.
construct.belief_after: V1 shows yellow mixture put inside a dough cup and the edges closed. The useful guide must teach a filled-dough flatbread, not merely plain bread or filling a cooked bread pocket.
construct.required_behavior_change: A model that saved a plain-only guide would need to change it after V1, but a complete applicable course already available after V0 needs no change. This conditional failure surface is not evidence of update necessity and does not qualify the candidate.
construct.no_update_failure: An initially reasonable plain-only choice remains after the raw-dough stuffing and sealing is revealed. Initial guides that already teach stuffing need no replacement.
construct.overupdate_failure: Discard an already applicable general tutorial because its filling, shape or heating apparatus differs; or save an extra plain guide as well as the required filled one.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The source images still distinguish the requested flatbread from instruction-only alternatives. However V0 alone leaves only the relevant plain/filled rolled-dough branches, and the real Paul Hollywood course m_664a1837b8f3 teaches both. V1 is not necessary to obtain a guaranteed legal complete final state; this proposal does not qualify as a Refresh-replace task.

catalog_resolution.answer_boundary_rule: Accept useful rolled/solid-dough flatbread foundations initially; later require useful instruction placing filling inside raw dough and enclosing it before cooking. No exact filling ingredient, regional identity, fold geometry, size, flour or heat-source restriction. A guide can contain additional recipes; accept it if at least one taught method satisfies the current requirement.

visual_necessity_counterexample.finding: No-scene necessity and later-update necessity have different conditioning information. Paul does not cover every instruction-only flatbread family, so it does not refute no_scene. After V0 has already established rolled griddle dough, it does cover both actual remaining plain/filled branches. It is therefore a demonstrated static substitute for V1, and the later-update necessity claim is withdrawn.
